transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… what brings me in is that I just cannot seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I’m a carpenter, so there’s always noise and movement around, but it’s gotten to where one saw starting up, or somebody walking past the office door, or even just me having a thought about another job I need to look at—any little thing like that pulls me right off whatever I was doing.

And then I’m not just briefly distracted, you know? The whole day sort of gets away from me. I’ll be in the middle of something, and suddenly I’m thinking about something else, or checking something else, and then I look back and realize I’ve lost track of what I was supposed to be doing in the first place. It’s really frustrating.
Did you have trouble paying attention like this when you were a child?

Yes. Looking back, it was definitely there when I was little — grade school, before I was 12 for sure. I remember teachers telling my mother the same kind of thing over and over, that I was bright, I could understand the work, but I was “careless.” That word came up a lot.

I’d lose homework, or I’d do it and then not turn it in, or forget what the teacher had just told us to do. And I can still picture myself sitting there staring out the window while everyone else was finishing their seatwork. It wasn’t that I didn’t want to do it exactly — I just… my mind would drift off, and then suddenly class was moving on and I hadn’t finished. My mother heard about it plenty.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually up or unusually irritable for several days in a row?

I’m not sure I’d say “unusually up,” no. I mean, I’ve had good moods, and I’ve had times where I’m irritated — especially when I’m overwhelmed or things are piling up — but I don’t know that I’ve had several days where I felt like… abnormally energized or on top of the world or anything like that.

I guess with irritability, it’s hard to say because I can get frustrated, but it feels more like a reaction to what’s going on, not like a whole separate mood that comes over me for days. If you mean something where other people would say, “What’s gotten into you?” or it feels really out of character for days in a row, I can’t think of a time like that.
Does this problem with losing focus cause trouble for you outside of work too?

Yes, it does. It’s not just work, though work is where it’s the most obvious because there’s money and other people waiting on me.

At home it’s… honestly, it’s embarrassing. My husband has had to take over a lot of the bills and the reminding, because I’ll put a paper down somewhere “safe” and then it’s just gone. Or I’ll mean to pay something, or call somebody back, or handle some form, and then I don’t do it because I got pulled into something else and it just disappears from my mind. Then later there’s a notice or a late fee or he’s asking me if I ever took care of it, and I haven’t.

And with work, it’s caused real problems. I’ve made mistakes that meant redoing parts of a job, or I’ve been late getting things ordered because I lost track of what needed to happen first. I’ve had delays that cost me commissions, and I can tell the crew doesn’t rely on me the same way for scheduling or ordering anymore. They’ll double-check me, or someone else will just take it over because they don’t want the job held up.

That part hurts, because I know my trade. I’m not careless about the quality because I don’t care — I do care. But the losing focus and misplacing things and missing the next step, it makes me look unreliable, and at home it’s made my husband have to manage things I feel like I should be able to handle.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?

I don’t know if I’d call it worrying about many different things. I mean, I worry some — everybody does, right? Bills, work, whether I forgot something important, things like that. But it’s usually tied to something that’s actually happening or something I know I might have dropped the ball on.

It doesn’t feel like I’m just sitting around worrying about every possible thing all day, if that’s what you mean. I can get stressed when there’s a mess to untangle or when I realize I missed something, but I’m not sure I’d describe myself as a big worrier in general.
Have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time lately?

I don’t think so… not depressed much of the time, no. I mean, I get discouraged, definitely. Especially when I mess something up or I realize I forgot something I said I’d do — then I can feel pretty low about myself for a while, like, “Why can’t I just keep track of normal things?” But it feels more like frustration or embarrassment than being depressed all the time.

I still have days where I’m okay, or I’m interested in what I’m doing, especially if I’m actually in the middle of a job and my hands are busy. I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down most of the day, every day, or anything like that. It’s more that I get worn out by the constant catching up and apologizing and trying to fix things. But depressed… I’m not sure that’s the word I’d use.
